title: International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2026/06
authors: Cohen, K.M.; Harper, D.A.T.; Gibbard, P.L.; Car, N.
note: Numerical ages are revision-prone; the atlas stores the exact chart version.

title: The Paleobiology Database application programming interface
authors: Peters, S.E.; McClennen, M.

title: Denormalized occurrence and taxon tables of the Paleobiology Database
authors: The Paleobiology Database Community; Kocsis, Á.T.
datasetSnapshot: PBDB full taxon table downloaded 2026-07-19; pbdb_taxa_csv.zip MD5 fca5fde5e8d5922d06fe332a42b955f9

title: Open Tree of Life web services
authors: OpenTreeOfLife Project
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: Using Phylogenomic Data to Explore the Effects of Relaxed Clocks and Calibration Strategies on Divergence Time Estimation: Primates as a Test Case
authors: dos Reis, M.; Gunnell, G.F.; Barba-Montoya, J.; Wilkins, A.; Yang, Z.; Yoder, A.D.
note: Open manuscript is available through PMC6005039. Node ages are Bayesian model outputs and vary with fossil-calibration strategy and relaxed-clock model.

title: Oldest known euarchontan tarsals and affinities of Paleocene Purgatorius to Primates
authors: Chester, S.G.B.; Bloch, J.I.; Boyer, D.M.; Clemens, W.A.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Open version of record at PMC4321231. The tarsals are isolated and attributed to Purgatorius by size, abundance and comparative morphology rather than dental association.

title: Altiatlasius koulchii n. gen. et sp., primate omomyidé du Paléocène supérieur du Maroc, et les origines des Euprimates
authors: Sigé, B.; Jaeger, J.-J.; Sudre, J.; Vianey-Liaud, M.
note: No DOI was located for the original description. The type series is about ten isolated teeth from Adrar Mgorn 1; tooth-locus assignments and broader placement have remained disputed.

title: A new family of plesiadapiformes (Mammalia) from the Old World lower Paleogene
authors: Hooker, J.J.; Russell, D.E.; Phélizon, A.
note: This primary systematic analysis recovers Altiatlasius within Toliapinidae rather than Euprimates. It is included as an explicit alternative placement, not as a replacement for the DOI-less original description.

title: Rapid Asia–Europe–North America geographic dispersal of earliest Eocene primate Teilhardina during the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum
authors: Smith, T.; Rose, K.D.; Gingerich, P.D.
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Open version of record at PMC1544069. The dispersal sequence is inferred from separate dental samples and intercontinental carbon-isotope correlation.

title: Evidence for a Grooming Claw in a North American Adapiform Primate: Implications for Anthropoid Origins
authors: Maiolino, S.A.; Boyer, D.M.; Bloch, J.I.; Gilbert, C.C.; Groenke, J.
note: Open-access version of record. The grooming-claw diagnosis is a comparative functional inference from preserved phalanges and statistical analyses.

title: Complete Primate Skeleton from the Middle Eocene of Messel in Germany: Morphology and Paleobiology
authors: Franzen, J.L.; Gingerich, P.D.; Habersetzer, J.; Hurum, J.H.; von Koenigswald, W.; Smith, B.H.
note: Open-access version of record at PMC2683573. PMO 214.214 and WDC-MG-210 are part and counterpart of one skeleton; the paper discloses fabricated preparation around portions of the counterplate.

title: The oldest known anthropoid postcranial fossils and the early evolution of higher primates
authors: Gebo, D.L.; Dagosto, M.; Beard, K.C.; Qi, T.; Wang, J.
note: The paper describes isolated Shanghuang tarsals and a Yuanqu talus attributed to eosimiids; none is dentally associated with Eosimias.

title: New Oligocene primate from Saudi Arabia and the divergence of apes and Old World monkeys
authors: Zalmout, I.S.; Sanders, W.J.; MacLatchy, L.M.; Gunnell, G.F.; Al-Mufarreh, Y.A.; Ali, M.A.; Nasser, A.-A.H.; Al-Masari, A.M.; Al-Sobhi, S.A.; Nadhra, A.O.; Matari, A.H.; Wilson, J.A.; Gingerich, P.D.
note: The holotype is one partial cranium. Its 29–28 Ma age is biochronological and its stem-catarrhine position is a morphology-matrix result.

title: Postcranial functional morphology of Morotopithecus bishopi, with implications for the evolution of modern ape locomotion
authors: MacLatchy, L.; Gebo, D.; Kityo, R.; Pilbeam, D.
note: MUZM 60 is from Moroto I and MUZM 80 from Moroto II. Their attribution and locomotor reconstruction are locality-level comparative interpretations, not one skeleton or observed behaviour.

title: A Complete Skull from Dmanisi, Georgia, and the Evolutionary Biology of Early Homo
authors: Lordkipanidze, D.; Ponce de León, M.S.; Margvelashvili, A.; Rak, Y.; Rightmire, G.P.; Vekua, A.; Zollikofer, C.P.E.
note: D4500 and D2600 are associated as Skull 5. The broad single-lineage interpretation of early Homo is an analysis of variation and remains distinct from the specimen observation.

title: A high-coverage Neandertal genome from Vindija Cave in Croatia
authors: Prüfer, K.; de Filippo, C.; Grote, S.; Mafessoni, F.; Korlević, P.; Hajdinjak, M.; Vernot, B.; Skov, L.; Hsieh, P.; Peyrégne, S.; et al.
note: Open manuscript at PMC6185897. The specimen has a direct radiocarbon lower bound; the approximately 52 ka age and demographic histories are genome-based model estimates.

title: Genome sequence of a 45,000-year-old modern human from western Siberia
authors: Fu, Q.; Li, H.; Moorjani, P.; Jay, F.; Slepchenko, S.M.; Bondarev, A.A.; Johnson, P.L.F.; Aximu-Petri, A.; Prüfer, K.; de Filippo, C.; et al.
note: Open manuscript at PMC4753769. PRJEB6622 contains the sequence data; the date is direct radiocarbon calibration, whereas ancestry and admixture timing are model estimates.

title: Major Questions in the Study of Primate Origins
authors: Silcox, M.T.; López-Torres, S.
publisher: Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences
note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of competing primate-origin, plesiadapiform and early euprimate hypotheses; it preserves disagreement over membership and ancestral ecology.

title: Macroevolutionary Dynamics and Historical Biogeography of Primate Diversification Inferred from a Species Supermatrix
authors: Springer, M.S. et al.
note: Primary 69-nuclear-segment and 10-mitochondrial-sequence supermatrix analysis of 367 living primate species; topology and ancestral-area results are bounded to that sample and taxonomy.

title: Catalogue of Life 2026-08-20 (COL26.8), ChecklistBank dataset 316115
authors: Catalogue of Life
note: Pinned checklist source for accepted usage identity and parent classification; it is not a fossil-range, wild-distribution or biological-trait source.

title: Fathering style influences health outcome in common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) offspring
authors: Ziegler, T.E.; Sosa, M.E.; Colman, R.J.
note: Primary study of offspring survival and growth among common marmosets housed at the Wisconsin National Primate Research Center. Only the captive-colony comparison is summarized; it does not estimate wild behavior or distribution.

title: Losing its ground: A case study of fast declining populations of a ‘least-concern’ species, the bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata)
authors: Erinjery, J.J.; Kumar, S.; Kumara, H.N.; Mohan, K.; Dhananjaya, T.; Sundararaj, P.; Kent, R.; Singh, M.
note: Primary study supporting bounded forest occupancy, temple/tourist-site history, Mysore roadside counts and a local conservation recommendation. Each finding retains its place, time and sample limits; none is a current range-wide assessment. Article states CC BY 4.0.

title: Activity and Habitat Use of Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes verus) in the Anthropogenic Landscape of Bossou, Guinea, West Africa
authors: Bryson-Morrison, N.; Tzanopoulos, J.; Matsuzawa, T.; Humle, T.
note: One-year field study of the wild Pan troglodytes verus community at Bossou, Guinea. Study claims are bounded to the sampled site and focal individuals. Article license and attribution were checked from the University of Kent repository record; the dossier paraphrases findings and reproduces no figures or tables. CC BY 4.0.

title: Primates, Provisioning and Plants: Impacts of Human Cultural Behaviours on Primate Ecological Functions
authors: Sengupta, A.; McConkey, K.R.; Radhakrishna, S.
note: Primary study of one 64-individual rhesus macaque troop at Buxa Tiger Reserve, India, from October 2013 to September 2014. Ecological comparisons are limited to that troop and study-defined seasonal provisioning periods; the article states CC BY 4.0.

title: Male morphological traits are heritable but do not predict reproductive success in a sexually-dimorphic primate
authors: Kimock, C.M.; Dubuc, C.; Brent, L.J.N.; Higham, J.P.
note: Primary study measuring a selected Cayo Santiago free-ranging cohort in 2015. Heritability conclusions are bounded to the sampled pedigree, measured traits and models; the article states CC BY 4.0.

title: Road-based line distance surveys overestimate densities of olive baboons
authors: Kiffner, C.; Paciência, F.M.D.; Henrich, G.; Kaitila, R.; Chuma, I.S.; Mbaryo, P.; Knauf, S.; Kioko, J.; Zinner, D.
note: Primary study of road-transect surveys and sleeping-site comparison for wild olive baboons at Lake Manyara National Park, Tanzania, from 2011 to 2019. The authors report poor fit for detection models and caution that road use may bias density estimates. The article states CC BY 4.0; the summary is paraphrased.

title: Segmental morphometrics of the olive baboon (Papio anubis): a longitudinal study from birth to adulthood
authors: Druelle, F.; Aerts, P.; D’Août, K.; Moulin, V.; Berillon, G.
note: Longitudinal body-morphometry study of 14 female and 16 male captive olive baboons at the CNRS Primatology Station in Rousset-sur-Arc, France. The source record identifies CC BY 4.0; the summary is paraphrased and does not reproduce figures or tables.

title: Contrasting effects of male immigration and rainfall on rank-related patterns of miscarriage in female olive baboons
authors: Bailey, A.; Eberly, L.E.; Packer, C.
note: Primary observational study of wild olive baboons in Gombe National Park, Tanzania, using reproductive and miscarriage records from 1972 to 2002. The article states CC BY 4.0; its conditional associations are not evidence of a species-wide rate or deliberate causation.

title: Pre-Historic and Recent Vicariance Events Shape Genetic Structure and Diversity in Endangered Lion-Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats: Implications for Conservation
authors: Ram, M.S.; Marne, M.; Gaur, A.; Kumara, H.N.; Singh, M.; Kumar, A.; Umapathy, G.; et al.
note: Primary mitochondrial-DNA study using wild Western Ghats samples, with separately identified captive samples in some analyses. Claims are bounded to sampled sites and markers; the article states CC BY 4.0.

title: Changing ecologies, shifting behaviours: Behavioural responses of a rainforest primate, the lion-tailed macaque Macaca silenus, to a matrix of anthropogenic habitats in southern India
authors: Dhawale, A.K.; Kumar, M.A.; Sinha, A.
note: Primary field study of one habituated, free-ranging troop in Puthuthottam, Valparai plateau, Tamil Nadu, during February–May 2016. Findings are bounded to one troop, one forest fragment and the dry season; the article states CC BY 4.0.

title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of rabies and habitat suitability of the common marmoset Callithrix jacchus in Brazil
authors: Benavides, J.A.; Raghavan, R.K.; Boere, V.; et al.
note: Primary analysis of Brazilian Ministry of Health passive surveillance from 2008 to 2020 and a presence-based habitat-suitability model. Reported cases, observed localities and modeled suitability are distinct evidence; none is a species-wide census or complete range inventory. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0.

title: Mitogenomic phylogeny of Callithrix with special focus on human transferred taxa
authors: Malukiewicz, J.; Cartwright, R.A.; Curi, N.H.A.; et al.
note: Primary Callithrix mitogenomic study combining 49 newly sequenced mitogenomes with published sequences. The approximately 0.51 Ma estimate concerns sampled mitochondrial lineages under the study model, not a nuclear-genome species tree or definitive species-origin date. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0.

title: Homo sapiens-specific evolution unveiled by ancient southern African genomes
authors: Jakobsson, M.; Bernhardsson, C.; McKenna, J.; et al.
note: Primary whole-genome study of 28 ancient southern African individuals dated 10,200–150 calibrated years before present. Genetic comparisons are bounded to the study samples and comparison panel, not a species-wide survey. Article text is item-level verified CC BY 4.0; summaries are paraphrased and figures, third-party content and data files are not reused.
